description: core §4.2, a conditional read's reader: which held stamp it sends, and what it holds after its GET's answer. Computed twice, by two readings of the text that shared no code, never blessed. A stamp is `{width, run, seq}`, as `inband.json` writes one, and a page is as `snapshot/bodies.json` reads one. `asks`: what a reader holds for one member → the held stamp it may send, `expect.held` with its bytes in `expect.hex`, or `{"held": null}` where it sends none. `holds` is `null`, or `{key, sample, stamp, record}` as a `view` entry below; a value with no envelope has `stamp` `null` and its Zenoh timestamp in `zenoh`. A case may give instead `page`, a snapshot's page the reader read on `key`, with its bytes in `hex`, and `member`, an id: what it holds is that id's entry, live or tombstone, or nothing where the page lists none. The held stamp is the in-band stamp of the mutation held: the entry's own run or the header's, and the entry's seq, never the asof. `cases`: `collections`, `view`, `arrivals`, `expect.view` and `expect.snapshots` are `snapshot.json`'s, with its merge and its omission rule. `asked` is the GET: its `key`, the selector, and `held`, the held stamp it carried, or `null` for a GET with no payload. An arrival may be a held stamp, `held` with its bytes in `hex`. It is the owner's answer when it arrives by the GET, the GET carried a held stamp on one concrete key (a selector with no `*`), the arrival's key is that key, and its stamp is the one the GET carried, in width, run and seq. Any other is refused as `held`: it merges nothing, and counts as nothing heard. An answer merges nothing either, and the reader keeps what it holds. Where the reader holds the mutation the stamp names when the answer arrives, that mutation counts as heard after the GET was asked, for the omission rule's guard. Where it holds another value by then, that value stands. Where it holds nothing for the member by then, `expect.read_again` is true: the GET gave it no value. `expect.held`: each held stamp among the arrivals, in order: `unchanged` for the owner's answer, or `held`, the refusal's token. Case 29, of core 0.116, was written by hand from the text and read against the reference's merge, not computed twice.

asks.note: a put held with its envelope's stamp
a deletion held: its delete's attachment's stamp
nothing held for the member: no held stamp
a value with no envelope, ordered by its Zenoh timestamp alone: no held stamp, and never one made of the timestamp
a member read by a snapshot: the entry's seq under the header's run, never the asof, 9
an entry with its own run: the entry's run, never the header's
an entry with its own 32-bit run under a 16-bit header
a tombstone read by a snapshot: the delete's stamp
a snapshot of no entry: nothing held, no held stamp, and never its asof
a collection's snapshot: each member's own entry's stamp

cases.note: unchanged: the owner answers the held stamp the GET carried. The reader keeps what it holds, and merges nothing
unchanged, a 32-bit run
unchanged, a deletion held: the member is still deleted, within its owner's window
unchanged, a template with no parameter: its one member's key is a concrete key
changed: a snapshot in answer, the member put again at seq 9. It merges as any member read's
changed: the member deleted within the window. The snapshot's tombstone merges as a delete
a delete beyond the window: a snapshot of no entry, the owner's word, drops the held put
a held deletion past its window: a snapshot of no entry drops it too, and the member holds nothing
an owner that reads no payload answers whole: the entry is the mutation the reader holds, kept once
another run: the owner restarted and put the member again. Its snapshot is another run's value, kept as the later arrival
another run, and the new instance holds no member: its snapshot of no entry drops a value held from before the GET
a stray held stamp: the GET carried none. No answer, though it names the mutation the reader holds
a stray held stamp for a member the reader holds nothing for: it merges nothing
a held stamp at another seq than the GET carried
a held stamp under another run than the GET carried
the run's value at the other width is another run: no answer
a held stamp heard on a subscription is no owner's answer, though it is the one the GET carried
a GET over a wildcard carried a held stamp: a held stamp in reply answers no one concrete key
a held stamp on another key than the GET's
a later value stands: a put heard while the GET was out, then the answer. Unchanged was true when the owner answered, and steps nothing back
a read is one instant: the owner answers unchanged, then puts. The put arrives by the subscription
another run's value heard while the GET was out, then the answer: the reader keeps the later value, where a snapshot of the old run would have replaced it
a delete heard while the GET was out, then the answer: the deletion stands
two instances answer, unchanged first: the mutation counts as heard again by the GET, so the other run's snapshot of no entry spares it
the same two answers in the other order: the snapshot of no entry drops a value held from before the GET, and the answer then finds nothing held. The reader reads again, with no held stamp
two instances answer, and the second lists the member under its own run: the later arrival is kept
unchanged, then a stray held stamp at another seq in the same GET: one answer and one refusal
a snapshot in answer whose entry carries its own run: the member was last put under the run the reader holds, and the header's run is the owner's now. The same mutation, kept once
a held stamp answers its member alone: another member the reader holds is untouched

the answer finds nothing held, so the reader reads again: a put heard after it, before the GET ends, changes nothing of that. "By then" is when the answer arrives (core §4.2). Written by hand for core 0.116
